summary: Choose r with ‖ℓ‖ ∨ ℓ^{−δ} < r^{q+L+ℓ+ma} < 1. Then build ζ coordinate by coordinate: replacing the j-th coordinate of u by a root of unity z keeps every F_{k,d} large (Gauss norm argument, exists_root_of_unity_eval_large applied to one-variable restrictions) and makes ∏ D_n(z) large; induction over the coordinates gives ζ.

steps.claim: If x^d = y_j, then G(y) is the value at x − 1 of G with the j-th variable replaced by (1 + X)^d and the others by the constants y_i.

steps.claim: By induction on the polynomial G.

Choose z, an ℓ^N-th root of unity, at which the one-variable polynomials (in X = x − 1) obtained from ∏ D_n (shifted: taylor) and from the F_{k,d} restricted to the j-th coordinate have values at least r^L and ℓ^{−B_k} r^{|s|+1}: their Gauss norms of radius r are that large, since otherwise the value at u_{k,d,j} − 1 (divisible by a root of (X^d − u)^a, of norm < r^n) would be too small (pow_le_norm_aeval).
